problem_type: generation result history tray viewport collision
symptom: On the constrained Linux desktop viewport, opening the version tray for a video node near the right canvas edge placed most of the tray outside the interactive stage, so the historical video and its controls were not visibly usable.
direct_cause: NodeResultStack used an unconditional right-side absolute offset without measuring the node, tray, or canvas-stage bounds.
class_root: Node-relative canvas overlays lacked the invariant that their resolved placement must use available stage space and avoid the viewport edge rather than assuming the preferred side always fits.
affected_population: Desktop users opening result history for a node near the right canvas edge
Users on constrained windows or Linux virtual displays where the requested window size is clamped
Video-history users who need the hover player, scrubber, preview, download, or delete controls
entry_points: CardStackPeeks version-count trigger for image nodes
CardStackPeeks version-count trigger for video nodes
NodeResultStack opening after canvas pan, zoom, fit-view, or constrained-window layout
internal_only_reason: This is an internal Nomi canvas geometry and interaction invariant. Third-party documentation cannot decide the stage boundary, preferred side, or fallback behavior for Nomi's node-relative history tray; the production DOM measurements and Linux Electron artifact are the deciding evidence.
invariants: The result tray prefers the right side when the measured stage space is sufficient.
The result tray flips to the left when the right side collides and the left side can contain it.
When neither side fully fits, placement chooses the side with more measured stage space.
The real Electron journey proves the opened tray is fully contained by the interactive canvas stage before exercising history media controls.

recurrence.reason: Any result tray opened near a stage edge or inside a constrained window could collide because the previous placement ignored measured space.
same_class_scan: Scanned every NodeResultStack entry from image and video card-stack peeks and the shared node-relative tray implementation.
Exercised right-side fit, left-side flip, and neither-side-fits geometry boundaries in the placement helper.
Ran the image and video history Electron journey at wide and constrained stage sizes and checked containment before media interaction.

prevention.strategy: Resolve the tray side from measured node, tray, and stage geometry whenever the result stack opens.

migration: No project, node, result-history, or media schema changes are required. Placement remains transient UI state and is recomputed whenever the tray opens.
residual_risks: At an unsupported window size where neither side can contain the tray, the larger side is chosen but the fixed-width tray may still be partially clipped.
Placement is recomputed on open; moving an already-open node across the viewport is currently hidden by the shared canvas-dragging contract rather than continuously repositioned.
